examShortTricks: Trick 1: The four similes are the poem — rose (beauty), melody (sweetness), the seas drying (eternity), the flower of June (youth); each simile = one mark in analysis.
Trick 2: Hyperbole question: 'till a' the seas gang dry' and 'rocks melt wi' the sun' are deliberate exaggerations of eternal love — name the device and its effect.
Trick 3: Dialect note: 'bonnie', 'gang', 'wi'' — Scots dialect adds intimacy and folk-song quality; mention it for the style mark.
practiceQuestions: Q. What two things does the speaker compare his love to? (2 marks) — a red rose and a sweet melody.
Q. Why does the speaker use exaggeration? (1 mark) — to express the boundless, eternal nature of his love.
keyPoints: Similes drive the poem: love compared to a red rose and a sweet melody.
Theme: eternal love — 'till a' the seas gang dry' uses hyperbole for devotion.
